text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- The government would like the parliament to debate a package of electoral law amendments in September, a senior Interior Ministry official said.
- The former Christian Democrat parliamentary group, which dissolved recently, met Thursday but was unable to reach a decision on how to continue their political career.
- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin described the conduct of anti-Hungarian nationalist Cluj Mayor Gheorghe Funar as extremely dangerous and secessionist.
NEPSZAVA
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and President Arpad Goncz cabled their condolences to their counterparts in Israel regarding Wednesday's suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- A full-scale no-visa agreement is due to take effect shortly between Hungary and Paraguay, the Foreign Ministry said. It also said that citizens from the Benelux states and Italy will soon be able to enter Hungary by prseneting only their identity cards.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- The Hungarian Export-Import Bank granted a $10 million medium-term credit line to the Moscow-based Inkombank.
- Police have confiscated hundreds of kilogramms of false Pick salami from several markets in Budapest.
- An international banking consortium, ,led by ABN AMRO signed a 168 million ECU guarantee for investment loans taken up by Hungarian telecom Matav Rt.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The signing of a $150 million World Bank loan to help the reform Hungary's higher education sector is expected for the autumn, Culture and Education Minister Balint Magyar said.
- The state privatisation agency APV is negotiating with potential investors into the three coal-run power plants Balonyi, Vertes and Pecsi.
- The Budapest Stock Exchange approved the listing of bus manufacturer NABI on Friday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The chemicals company TVK earned eight billion forints after-taxprofit, an unexpected record, on net sales of 40 billion forints in the firts half of 1997.
- Drug maker Richter earned profits of 7.7 billion forints on sales of 24.8 billion forints in the first half of the year, CEO Elek Bogsch said.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Chemicals Borsodchem annnounced lukewarm first half results. The unaudited first half balance sheet shows pre-taxearnings of 4.4 billion forints, up from 4.1 billion in the same period of last year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- An Agricultural Ministry official said that half of the country's wheat crop had been harvested and denied reports of a sharp decline in wheat quality.
- The 1998 central budget has for the firts time a separate chapter for the costs of preparations for European Union and NATO membership, allocating 14.9 billion forints for that.
